summary: Enterprise Suite AC-16 adds a declarative Kubernetes/GitOps deployment manifest foundation and composes it into the cloud-readiness gate. The manifest validates namespace, digest-pinned image reference, probe paths, resource requests and limits, replica bounds, ArgoCD/Jenkins/Cosign/network/OTel references, and explicit non-claims while refusing imperative deploy flags or runtime attachment overclaims.

findings: The new crate is a typed manifest validator with no side effects, no provider clients, and no network or filesystem runtime path.
Failure modes are explicit enum variants instead of stringly readiness booleans.
The slice advances cloud integration readiness by making Kubernetes, ArgoCD, Jenkins, Cosign, network policy, OTel, and SLO surfaces machine-checkable before any deployment claim.

Cloud readiness remains false because runtime blockers for listener, auth, durable storage, Postgres/RLS, Workflow/broker, statutory rails, runtime audit, deployment evidence, and production SLO evidence are still present.

F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Tests fail if the manifest allows imperative kubectl or Helm deploys, mutable image tags, unsafe refs, weak replica/resource/probe/SLO values, or runtime attachment claims.
findings: Positive manifest validation and negative overclaim, image, ref, replica, resource, probe, and SLO validations are covered.
Developers can call enterprise_suite_cloud_deployment_manifest() and validate_cloud_deployment_manifest() to see the required pre-cloud deployment contract and rejection reasons.

Targeted manifest check/test/clippy, cloud-readiness test/clippy, 36-package enterprise regression test/clippy, fmt, jq, data_class scan, quality-marker scan, dependency-seam gate, Oya VCS verify/done/promote, and audit-chain append-only checks are required for closeout.

alternatives_named: claim cloud readiness from the existing readiness gate alone
add real Kubernetes manifests and a live ArgoCD application now
add a typed declarative manifest foundation without deployment claims
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: A typed foundation gives later cloud work a narrow, testable contract while avoiding false deployment, image publication, or controller-attachment claims.
rejected_reasons: The existing readiness gate did not model deployment manifest policy, image pinning, imperative deploy refusal, probe/resource bounds, or GitOps references.

Live deployment would be premature because auth, durable storage, Workflow/broker, statutory rails, runtime audit emission, deployment evidence, and production SLO evidence remain unresolved blockers.

findings: No secrets, tenant data, listener, auth runtime, cloud provider SDK, service account creation, image signing key, or cluster credential is introduced.
Reference validators reject unsafe text, path traversal, credential-shaped refs, default/system namespaces, mutable images, and imperative deployment flags.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: Validation checks a fixed in-memory manifest with scalar fields and static refs; no I/O, network calls, provider clients, or hot request path exists.

findings.summary: Manifest validation is bounded by a fixed set of fields and does not affect runtime throughput.

findings: All public struct fields in changed source carry data_class annotations.
The manifest keeps statutory filing and disbursement rails out of scope and keeps runtime audit emission as an unresolved cloud blocker.
The change is additive: one crate, one catalog row, spec/task/evidence updates, and a readiness-gate composition field. No migration or external resource is created.
The readiness report now includes a cloud_deployment_manifest_ready flag and evidence ref for dashboard and release-gate consumption.
Runtime OTel export and deploy audit emission remain explicit non-claims.
Enterprise Suite AC-16 records a staged migration boundary from local manifest foundation to later cloud deployment work.
The readiness gate incorporates the manifest without removing the remaining cloud blockers.

M1_challenge_assumption.premise_stated: A declarative manifest foundation is useful before a real Kubernetes or ArgoCD deployment only if it refuses runtime attachment claims and imperative deployment paths.
M1_challenge_assumption.premise_evidence_ref: manifest.rs negative tests plus cloud readiness gate blocker assertions
M1_challenge_assumption.do_nothing_consequence: Later cloud work would need to infer deployment expectations from prose instead of consuming a typed, tested policy record.
M1_challenge_assumption.upstream_fix_rejection_reason: The cloud-readiness gate owns aggregate status, but a separate manifest crate keeps deployment policy validation isolated from readiness aggregation.

findings: This is the next smallest cloud-integration step after ERP parity closure: it provides a GitOps deployment contract while preserving the no-cloud-deployment boundary.
Names use cloud-deployment-manifest vocabulary and avoid deployed-service or production-ready claims.
Enterprise Suite spec, plan, todo, catalog, multispectrum evidence, VCS evidence, and audit-chain references are part of the closeout set.
The crate sits under microservices/enterprise-suite/crates with a product-control catalog row and no new runtime adapter layer.
No listener, auth runtime, durable store, Postgres/RLS, provider SDK, Workflow engine/broker, child-service network client, cloud adapter, statutory rail, or runtime audit emitter was introduced.
The new manifest crate has no third-party dependencies; the readiness gate adds only a local workspace dependency on it.
No external wire API schema changes; the addition is a Rust control-plane struct plus Enterprise Suite AC-16 metadata.
Validation is deterministic scalar/ref checking with no clock, randomness, I/O, network, or provider calls.
